name: bugpilot
//description: Both ways in, equally: a Jira issue or a bug described by hand. The old line said 'a Jira bug' only, while most first runs need no Jira at all.
description: Turn a Jira issue or a bug you describe into focused code context for your AI coding agent, without leaving the editor.
//icon: The Marketplace and Extensions-list image. Must be a PNG - vsce refuses an SVG outright - and is drawn by scripts/make-icon.mjs so it can be regenerated rather than being an unexplained binary. Not the activity bar icon; that one is contributes.viewsContainers.activitybar[0].icon.
//license: See LICENSE.txt for the parameterized BUSL 1.1 terms.
//categories: `Programming Languages` was wrong and was there: that category is for extensions that add language support - grammars, servers, debuggers - and browsing it for this would waste the reader's time. A category is a shelf in someone else's shop, not a keyword.
//keywords: What someone looking for this would type, and no more: the agents it hands work to by name, the two ways a bug arrives, and what it builds. No company, product or domain words.
//engines: vscode is the minimum API level, pinned to @types/vscode so no newer API can be used by accident. node 22.18 is where type stripping landed, which the test script relies on.
//main: The extension host requires CommonJS JS, so the packaged entry point is built by tsconfig.build.json. Tests run the TypeScript sources directly instead.
//menus: Comments for contributes.menus live here: VS Code reads every key inside `menus` as a menu id, so a comment there is reported as a submenu that is not an array. commandPalette: bugpilot.openArtifact and bugpilot.showWorkItem are invoked by a tree item with an argument; from the palette they would have nothing to act on. view/item/context: right-clicking a History row acts on that row: the handlers switch the panel to it first, so nothing happens invisibly to a different work item. `viewItem` keeps the menu off the placeholder rows, the artifact rows and the Current and History group rows.
//views: Results is one native tree with two groups, Current (the open work item's artifacts) and History, rather than two views. VS Code gives every expanded view the same minimum height whatever it holds, so a one-line Artifacts and a one-row History cost that twice; one view costs it once. `initialSize` is VS Code's weight for a view's first height in a container the same extension owns (each gets height * weight / total): Workflow 100, Results 1: Results asks for a sliver, so VS Code gives it its own minimum for an open view (a 28px header and a 120px body) and Workflow everything else, however tall the window. 10 to 1 did that only up to about 1700px, and left Results 181px in a 2100px window (dev plan 37.111). It applies only while the profile has no saved size for the view: once someone drags the sash, VS Code keeps their sizes, and nothing here overrides them. `visibility` is said outright: both views start expanded.
//capabilities: Declared rather than left to the default. This extension spawns a process whose path a workspace can override (bugpilot.executablePath), so it has no business running in a folder the developer has not trusted - VS Code already disables it there, and saying so gives the reason instead of silent inaction. It also reads and writes the filesystem and runs a local CLI, none of which exists in a virtual workspace.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: BugPilot runs the bugpilot CLI, and a workspace can point bugpilot.executablePath at a file inside itself.

virtualWorkspaces.description: BugPilot runs a local CLI and reads the repository from disk.

bugpilot.executablePath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `bugpilot` executable; when set, it is the only one used. Leave empty to use the BugPilot runtime if it is installed, otherwise to find `bugpilot` on `PATH` (its absolute entries only, never the workspace folder). A relative path is refused.

scripts.package: npm run build && node scripts/check-package.mjs && vsce package --no-dependencies
